results.name: Atlas Raises $6 Million Seed Round | The SaaS News
results.content:
Atlas, a Singapore-based technology company, has raised $6 million in a Seed funding round.  
**Investors**  
The round was co-led by Accel and Stellaris Venture Partners.  
Founded in 1983 and headquartered in Palo Alto, Accel is a global venture capital firm that partners with exceptional founders from inception through all phases of growth. The firm has backed category-defining technology companies across consumer, enterprise, and infrastructure sectors, following a long-term, founder-centric approach. Accel operates globally, investing across North America, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia.  
Stellaris Venture Partners is a prominent early-stage venture capital firm headquartered in Bengaluru, India. The firm focuses primarily on early-stage investments in technology-driven startups. With over $600 million in assets under management, Stellaris typically invests at the pre-seed, seed, and Series A stages, often acting as one of the first institutional investors in a company’s journey.  
**Atlas Use of Funds**  
The company plans to use the funds to scale its AI-driven accounting platform, expand partnerships with accounting firms across North America, and accelerate its go-to-market efforts.  
**About Atlas**
**About Atlas**  
Founded in 2025 by Arpit Maheshwari and Jagmal Singh, Atlas is a technology company developing an AI-driven platform to support accounting firms by embedding automation across delivery and administrative workflows. The company partners with independent accounting firms to help them scale efficiently, improve margins, and deliver higher-quality client outcomes. Headquartered in Singapore, Atlas’s mission is to help accounting firms build more sustainable businesses.  
**Funding Details**

Lead Investors: Accel, Stellaris Venture Partners

results.name: Atlas Raises $6 Million in Seed Funding to Build AI Tools for Accounting Firms - Indian Startup Times
results.content:
AI-led accounting platform [Atlas](https://theatlas.ai/) has raised $6 million in a seed funding round, co-led by Accel and Stellaris Venture Partners. The fresh capital will be used to expand its AI platform, strengthen its presence in North America, and scale its go-to-market efforts.
#### Building AI for Modern Accounting Firms  
Founded in 2025 by Arpit Maheshwari and Jagmal Singh, Atlas is focused on developing AI-native tools for independent accounting firms. The platform is designed to automate workflows across both core delivery functions and administrative operations, helping firms improve efficiency.  
Atlas follows a human-in-the-loop approach, where AI assists accountants in executing tasks while allowing them to focus on more strategic and high-value work.
#### Expansion Plans Ahead  
With the new funding, Atlas plans to grow its network of partner accounting firms, deepen its product capabilities, and continue building solutions tailored to the evolving needs of the accounting industry.  
As AI adoption accelerates across professional services, Atlas is positioning itself to play a key role in transforming how accounting firms operate.  
*-By Shivani Solanki*

Atlas, a Singapore-headquartered technology company, announced it has raised $6 million in seed funding to advance its AI-driven accounting platform and expand its footprint in North America. The round was co-led by Accel and Stellaris, two early-stage venture capital firms, with the capital earmarked for product development, partner network growth, and go-to-market acceleration in a global accounting market valued at over $150 billion.

With the new funding, Atlas plans to deepen its AI capabilities, expand its network of partner accounting firms, particularly in North America, and accelerate adoption across the industry as firms look to scale operations without increasing headcount.
Atlas is building infrastructure that will allow the best independent firms to compete at a scale that was previously out of their reach. We are also putting skin in the game with our partners, aligning our incentives directly to their success. This funding allows us to deepen our platform, grow our network, and move with the urgency this moment demands.” Arpit Maheshwari, CEO, Atlas
